title: First-week exemplar: Skill snapshot + shadow pairing rota
content:
Purpose:
This note defines a compact, low-friction "first-week exemplar" for new IC hires (engineer / platform / SRE profiles) that blends a lightweight skills snapshot, a 1:1 shadow pairing rota, and a pragmatic acceptance checklist for people-ops + hiring manager handoffs. Goal: reduce time-to-autonomy for the first 7 days while keeping cognitive load low.

Why this exists:
- We repeatedly see variance in week-one experiences across pods: some new joiners get overloaded with tickets, others sit idle waiting on access.
- Short, measurable rituals (skill snapshot + 2-day shadow pairs) create predictable learning trajectories and better early signal for manager decisions.

High-level flow (summary):
1) Pre-boarding (48h before start): access request, intro packet, one tiny prework task (read architecture map + run local dev bootstrap).
2) Day 0 / Day 1: orientation + skills snapshot + buddy pairing schedule.
3) Days 2–4: focused shadow blocks (pairing) with agreed micro-tasks.
4) Days 5–7: first independent micro-ticket, demo, feedback loop and success signal.

Skills snapshot (10 min, manager + hire):
- Self-rated confidence (1–5) on core areas: codebase, infra, deploys, observability, incident response, API design.
- Recent similar work: 3 bullets (projects, languages, infra).
- One learning goal for first 30 days.

Interview rubric -> onboarding lens (used to prioritize early tasks):
- 0–2: Needs immediate pairing and access to documentation; avoid critical oncall tasks.
- 3: Pair with an experienced buddy for first two days; give read-only access where possible.
- 4–5: Assign small independent ticket with mentor review; ok for light rotation oncall shadow.

Week-one checklist (operational):
- Preboarding: AD account, laptop imaged, repo access, infra test project provisioned, Slack channel created, calendar invites for orientation.
- Day 0: welcome + HR intro, send welcome slack thread, intro to team rituals (standup, retro).
- Day 1 morning: skills snapshot (10m), security & access walkthrough (20m), local dev + successful test run (30–60m).
- Day 1 afternoon: pair with buddy on a curated read-only flow (observability dashboard walkthrough).
- Day 2–3: two 90m pairing blocks per day (deploy flow, feature trace, infra runbook).
- Day 4: small code or infra change in a sandbox (mentor reviews PR).
- Day 5–7: independent micro-ticket, 1:1 feedback at end of week, collection of blockers for people-ops and hiring manager.

Shadow pairing rota (example template):
- Buddy assignment: 1 primary buddy (same pod) + 1 secondary (cross-pod)
- Daily blocks (sample):
  - 09:30–11:00 onboarding pairing (buddy A)
  - 14:00–15:30 systems walkthrough (buddy B)
  - Ad-hoc 30m window for Q&A each afternoon
- Notes for buddies: keep sessions task-focused, end with a 3-item recap and one clear action for hire.

Mentor / Buddy quick reference (what to do in a pairing block):
- 10m: set expectation, what will be covered, outcome (observe / co-pilot / drive).
- 60–75m: live run-through (screen share), narrate decisions, point to docs and ticket history.
- 5–10m: 3 takeaways + next steps.

Acceptance criteria for first-week success (signals):
- Technical: successful local build + one sandbox PR opened and reviewed.
- Operational: able to follow deploy playbook and identify a key dashboard.
- Social: participated in at least one async thread and introduced themselves in team channel.

Common blockers (and mitigations):
- Missing infra access: escalate to infra with priority template (linked_artifact JIRA id in checklist).
- Overloaded schedule: drop nonessential meetings, preserve pairing blocks.
- Mentor bandwidth: fallback to secondary buddy or another in-pod engineer.

Lightweight hiring-plan tie-ins:
- If skills snapshot shows many 1–2s in critical infra, set 30-day plan to include targeted shadow rotations and a mid-month technical task.
- If snapshot shows 4–5 across core areas, accelerate to independent sprint tasks and set a 30-day stretch goal.

Feedback & data capture (people-ops):
- At EOW (end of week) collect: 3 short structured answers from hire (what helped, what blocked, top 1 suggestion) + buddy feedback (3 bullets).
- Store as a short entry in Confluence (template id: CONFLUENCE-1432) and tag manager for review.

Open questions / decisions needed (people-ops):
- Standardize primary buddy time budget per hire (current suggestion: 6 hours across first 3 days).
- Should we require the prework dev bootstrap for all non-intern hires? (ops impact: laptop imaging cadence).

References / links:
- JIRA onboarding template: JIRA-PLAT-982
- Confluence: onboarding micro-templates (CONFLUENCE-1432)
- Slack rituals: #people-ops onboarding pinned messages

Quick next steps (for people-ops owner):
- Pilot with 3 hires in September; collect EOW artefacts and run retro.
- Create one-card checklist for managers + one-pager for buddies.

Notes to self: keep language minimal, prefer checkboxes over essays, avoid forcing long meetings in week one.
